title: Current warmth slopes did not clearly exceed future warmth slopes in four UK beetle catch samples in 1993-2015
abstract: We tested whether beetle catches had a stronger link to current warmth than to future warmth. We used 3,054 selected ten-trap collections in England and Scotland in 1993-2003 and 2004-2015. Each model compared collection-period temperature with an equal-length window shifted 28 days later. Models controlled rain, duration, date, location by month and year. Current minus future slopes ranged from -0.100 to +0.137 log count plus one per degree C. All four adjusted year-cluster intervals included zero. Positive catches, short intervals, a 56-day shift and prior-weather control also gave intervals across zero. Half of the primary records shared a source weather month between windows. Thus future weather is an imperfect reference. Few years, coarse weather, trap selection and mixed activity and density limit inference. The result does not show that capture bias is absent or estimate a causal climate effect. The package gives code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, checks and a figure. It tests no pollution effect or weather extreme.

display.caption: Current and future temperature slopes and their direct difference in four selected beetle catch samples. All adjusted contrast intervals include zero.
